newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH ECONOMY THREATENED BY OVERHEATING - THINKTANK.
newsitem.headline: POLISH ECONOMY THREATENED BY OVERHEATING - THINKTANK.

text.p: Poland's economy risks overheating because of rising consumer credit, which should be contained by keeping interest rates unchanged or increasing them, a private think-tank said on Thursday.
Bogdan Wyznikiewicz of the Gdansk Free Market Economy Research Institute (IBnGR) said that households' debts with banks has increased by 90 percent in 1996.
"This is something that must be tamed, because it is one of the factors behind the economic overheating," he told a news conference.
IBnGR president Jan Szomburg, also present, said he expected the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, to increase its interest rates.
"A rate rise is quite probable, because current circumstances discourage people from putting money in bank accounts," Szomburg said.
Szomburg said the Polish economy was prone to overheating because the capital market was not sufficiently developed and provided little alternative to consumer spending.

Institute analysts also pointed to rising real wages, which according to official forecasts will increase by 5.6 percent in 1996, as a factor which could contribute to overheating. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
